subject: Storix Bank RFP: orchestration handoff + DB migration & traffic-splitting guidelines
messages:
From: Katie Miller <kmiller@storixbank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: eng-ops@storixbank.com; andrew.li@compass-consulting.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Storix RFP — detailed migration questionnaire & canary expectations

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick response to our RFP. As part of our procurement we need a detailed, step-by-step implementation/migration plan that covers sequencing, orchestration handoff, DB migration strategy (live vs. bulk), traffic-splitting rules for canary, rollback criteria, and post-cutover validation. Key constraints:

- Migration must avoid any customer-facing downtime during business hours (Eastern 8am–6pm)
- Data residency remains in us-east resources; any temporary caches must be flushed
- We require explicit p99 latency and token-loss thresholds for canary acceptance

Please provide a draft timeline (milestones and durations), integration touchpoints, what you need from our Eng Ops, and a short checklist for the first two canary waves. Also attach any runbooks or templates you use so our procurement & security teams can review.

Can you get an initial draft by EOD Wed?

Thanks,
Katie Miller
Senior Procurement Manager, Storix Bank
[kmiller@storixbank.com]

[Attachment requested: migration/runbook template]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Katie Miller <kmiller@storixbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Storix RFP — detailed migration questionnaire & canary expectations

Katie —

Thanks, this is very clear. I’ve attached a migration plan template and a short canary-validation checklist that we use in similar bank rollouts. High-level notes up front:

- We recommend a 3-phase migration:
  1) Pre-migration staging + end-to-end integration test (2–3 weeks)
  2) Controlled canary traffic split (4 waves over 2 weeks)
  3) Scale-up and full cutover with rollback windows (1 week)

- DB migration: prefer logical replication (CDC) with read-only cutover for the first wave to validate query patterns; full write cutover only after wave 3 acceptance. This minimizes business-hour risk.

- Canary pass criteria (example):
  • p99 inference latency < 250ms for production-like load
  • error rate < 0.2% (5xx or model-fusion failures)
  • no material degradation in token-level throughput or cost-per-token beyond 10% of baseline
  • qualitative check: key prompt regression set results within tolerance (sampled)

- Rollback: feature-flag toggles + immediate traffic re-route to fallback model cluster; DB failback plan if writes are involved.

I’ve included a draft timeline and a short list of integration touchpoints in the attached spreadsheet. Vivek and Laura — can you add infra-specific prereqs (network prep, KV cache warming steps, observability hooks) and call out expected Eng Ops inputs?

Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[jonas_weber@redwood.ai]

Attachments: redwood_migration_template.xlsx (xlsx), canary-validation-checklist.md (md)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Storix RFP — orchestration handoff and infra notes

Adding infra details below and inline in the spreadsheet. Key items for Storix Eng Ops:

1) Network & IAM
- Provide VPC peering details and a small service account for initial test traffic. We’ll use mTLS for control-plane calls and customer-managed keys for data-in-transit encryption.

2) DB migration approach (detailed)
- Phase A (staging): run schema compatibility checks; seed a 10% traffic shadow against staging store.
- Phase B (CDC): enable Debezium-style CDC into a materialized replica in the Redwood cluster. Reads are served from materialized replica; writes continue to primary for waves 1–2.
- Phase C (dual-write optional): if Storix wants full end-to-end verification before switching writes, enable dual-write for selected user segments for up to 72 hours, then promote replica.

3) Traffic splitting & orchestration
- Canary waves (suggested percentages): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% (then 100 on final cut). Each wave should be min 24h and include at least two business peak windows.
- Automated rollback triggers: sustained p99 > 300ms for 15 minutes OR error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes OR any security/audit exception. On trigger, traffic re-routes to the previous cluster within ~2 minutes.

4) Observability & validations (must-haves)
- Token-level tracing for sampled requests, p50/p95/p99 metrics, model output diffs against golden prompt set, and cost-per-call breakdowns.
- We’ll provide a short ELK/Kibana dashboard bundle and a Playbook section for incident runbook steps.

5) Operational handoff
- Handoff checklist: access verification, runbooks present in customer Drive link, SRE contact list, and a final blackout window agreed (we prefer 02:00–05:00 ET for final write promotion).

Notes: KV cache warming — we’ll pre-warm caches over a rolling window by replaying recent session prefixes (we can do this once Storix provides a sanitized sample).

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra | Redwood Inference
[vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai]

Team —

This is exactly the level of detail our procurement & security teams wanted. A few clarifications before we circulate to legal and security:

- Please add a short table that maps each canary wave to the exact observability artifact (dashboard ID) we should review.
- Confirm the blackout window for final write promotion (02:00–05:00 ET) and that your rollback completes within the stated ~2 minutes for traffic reroute.
- For CDC flow: confirm retention of the materialized replica’s logs for audit (90 days) and whether you support a tamper-evident log option.

Next steps: Marissa — can you produce a 1-page summary + the updated spreadsheet with the dashboard IDs and a proposed SOW stub? If we have that by EOD Friday we’ll move to a security review slot next week.

Thanks,
Katie
Senior Procurement Manager, Storix Bank
